scope: Targeted current-guidance resolution pass for remaining Endocrinology and Rheumatology conflicts with complete retained stems/options.
policy: Preserve recalledAnswer unchanged as source provenance.
Assign verifiedAnswer only when the retained stem/options support a defensible modern single-best answer.
Do not invent missing options, thresholds, images, or context.
If a precise numeric pattern is not uniquely diagnostic, retain the item as non-publishable rather than forcing certainty.

items.reason: McCune-Albright syndrome classically causes gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty from autonomous sex-steroid production. GnRH agonists treat central, GnRH-dependent precocious puberty and should not be expected to control the peripheral process unless secondary central puberty develops. The retained option A therefore correctly identifies the treatment that should not be automatically assumed to work for the peripheral process.
references: FD/MAS International Consortium best-practice management guideline

items.reason: JIA synovial fluid is usually inflammatory and typically remains below the very high neutrophilic counts seen in acute bacterial arthritis. Published JIA series report median synovial WBC around 11,757/mm3 with broad overlap, while pediatric bacterial arthritis commonly exceeds 50,000/mm3 and often 100,000/mm3 with neutrophil predominance. Among the retained choices, 8,000 WBC with 30% PMN is the best fit; however, the exact count/differential is not a diagnostic cutoff and must be interpreted with the clinical context.
references: Characteristics of synovial fluid in patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, 2019
PIDS/IDSA 2023 Acute Bacterial Arthritis in Pediatrics guideline
